DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.PURPOSE: Проект архитектурного графа GRACE: восемь предварительно согласованных модулей, вызовы, границы владения и последовательность работ. Утверждён командным центром; разрешена подготовка контрактов, но тесты и реализация только после их отдельного согласования.

MODULES.MODULE: BFE Auth integration: внутренний UDS validate, проверка текущей сессии; проверка ADMIN для административных операций, DPoP на клиентских соединениях.
Назначения: явный recipient_account_id, атомарная замена; без автоматического выбора администратора.
Переписки и сообщения: одна история на пользователя, идемпотентность и определение получателя при записи.
Разграничение доступа к истории, отправке, административному просмотру и смене получателя.
Centrifuge real-time доставка и OnConnecting; история сохраняется в PostgreSQL.
Контекст одного документа без передачи файлов и прав доступа.
PostgreSQL, pgx, goose: хранение, транзакции и миграции.
HTTP и WebSocket транспорт для Flutter Web, Android и административного UI.

BOUNDARIES.BOUNDARY: BFE Auth owns accounts, session lifecycle and ADMIN state. DP-M01 validates existing token via restricted Unix socket, independently verifies client DPoP and exposes request identity; it does not create accounts, tokens or sessions.

DP-M02 exclusively owns recipient assignment changes. Admin UI supplies an accountId selected from BFE Drive user list; assignment is stored in Chat Service, replacement is atomic and never automatic.
DP-M03 owns one conversation per user, message writes, idempotency and history. Persisting owner messages continues when the previously assigned recipient is blocked or deleted.

DP-M04 decides chat resource permissions using validated caller identity and current chat assignment. ADMIN is required only for administrative actions; audit-mode viewing remains read-only and never generates view-audit events.
DP-M05 owns transient connection/subscription/delivery state, not permanent messages or assignment. Centrifuge OnConnecting delegates token/DPoP validation to DP-M01 and permission checks to DP-M04.
DP-M06 validates and stores at most one provided document ID/title context per message; BFE Drive exclusively owns document content and its access controls.

DP-M07 is the sole persistence adapter for Chat Service data in PostgreSQL, including transactionally consistent assignment/message operations and migrations. No direct access to BFE Drive application tables is assumed.
DP-M08 owns external HTTP/WebSocket protocol boundaries only, not authentication policy, authorization decisions or business persistence.

DEPENDENCIES.convention: from-calls-to; runtime logical dependency, not Go import graph

FLOWS.FLOW: Flutter client - DP-M08 - DP-M01 - DP-M04 - DP-M03 - DP-M02/DP-M06 - DP-M07 commit - DP-M05 delivery; recipients are reauthorized against the current assignment, and no delivery precedes durable persistence.
Admin UI - DP-M08 - DP-M01 ADMIN - DP-M04 - DP-M02 - DP-M07 atomic assignment; former recipient loses access without rewriting history.
Admin UI - DP-M08 - DP-M01 ADMIN - DP-M04 audit-read permission - DP-M03 - DP-M07; no view-audit event or sending permission is created.
Flutter Web/Android WebSocket - DP-M08 - DP-M05 OnConnecting - DP-M01 BFE token via UDS plus DPoP - DP-M04 subscription authorization; history is fetched from DP-M03/DP-M07 after reconnect.

INTEGRATION_CONSTRAINTS.RULE: All eight modules belong to the single approved Go Chat Service process; graph edges are logical responsibilities and do not prescribe new network services.
Reuse approved Centrifuge, net/http, PostgreSQL, pgx and goose; do not add Redis, a separate broker, JWT, connection tickets or alternative Auth endpoints without new evidence and approval.
Protect the local BFE Auth Unix socket using approved OS access controls. Nginx and external HTTPS remain at the public ingress of the shared Ubuntu VPS.
Recipient blocking or deletion does not interrupt owner message persistence; the recipient is unable to authenticate through revoked sessions. A missing assignment still prevents sending.

IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.PHASE: After DevelopmentPlan approval, specify module boundaries and function contracts; independently validate authorization and ownership rules before implementation.
Specify storage schema, migration discipline, conversation/assignment integrity, transactional idempotency and concurrency behavior.
Specify BFE UDS Auth, ADMIN boundaries, DPoP OnConnecting, key binding, replay resistance and reconnection semantics.
Implement assignment, conversation, message, history and document context operations behind the reviewed contracts.
Implement Centrifuge subscriptions and post-commit delivery with authorization under reassignments; do not use its transient history as durable storage.
Run Flutter Web and Android integration tests for DPoP, replay, revoked sessions, reconnection and recipient access transitions.
Run approved acceptance checks; verify the shared VPS resource budget, PostgreSQL 18.6 compatibility, systemd, Nginx and socket permissions before deployment.

SEQUENCE.STEP: Согласовать контракты модулей, схему постоянных данных, атомарность назначений и идемпотентность.
Определить конкретную DPoP-проверку в Centrifuge OnConnecting: подпись, dpopJkt, ath, привязка proof к соединению, срок действия, replay и reconnect. Без JWT, новых сессий и билетов.
Проверить отправку активным владельцем после блокировки получателя; доступ заблокированного получателя запрещён, назначение не меняется автоматически.
Реализовать после одобрения контрактов операции назначения, переписки, сообщений, истории и доставки.
Интеграционные тесты Flutter Web и Android: DPoP, replay, истёкшие и отозванные сессии, переподключение, права.
Проверить Ubuntu VPS, PostgreSQL 18.6, systemd, Nginx и локальный Unix socket до развёртывания.

GATES.GATE: После утверждения плана подготовить контракты модулей и функций, затем тесты и реализацию согласно GRACE.

ISSUE25_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.DESIGN_BOUNDARIES: Same Go service and approved PostgreSQL bfe_chat / pgx / goose / embedded Centrifuge / net/http / existing UDS and DPoP. No dependency changes or BFE Drive mutations. API endpoints and schema migration are not implemented or approved.

MODULE.NAME: Identity and Chat authorization
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Validate caller via existing UDS/DPoP; resolve conversation membership/role from bfe_chat at protected operation boundary; reject on auth outage. Drive ADMIN has no automatic Chat permission.

MODULE.NAME: Conversation lifecycle
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Independent conversation_id UUID with kind DIRECT/GROUP; canonical unordered direct pair uniqueness; personal hidden flag for each direct participant; incoming message or explicit open restores visibility.

MODULE.NAME: Membership/roles/visibility
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Per-conversation membership epochs represented as half-open visibility intervals in committed message order; exactly one owner for groups; only owner changes admin; admin manages members only; leaving owner must transfer first.

MODULE.NAME: Durable messaging/history
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: PostgreSQL conversation-scoped ordered messages, immutable author/payload/document metadata, history filtered by union of user's membership intervals, keyset pagination and immutable persisted idempotency outcome.

MODULE.NAME: Realtime delivery
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Centrifuge delivers only minimal content-free wake-up to opaque conversation/viewer/never-reused membership-epoch channels. PostgreSQL transaction gate protects SEND/JOIN/REMOVE/TRANSFER and committed message order, not cancellation of external Publish. Pre-REMOVE Publish can complete after REMOVE or timeout, outcome UNKNOWN; NEW Publish attempts after removal are rejected. Subscription revocation best effort; every history read requires fresh authorization and membership interval check. No sensitive content in envelope, channel IDs, or recoverable history.

MODULE.NAME: Read states
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Durable per-account/conversation monotonic last-read marker; unread counts only committed visible other-authored messages after marker, excluding intervals of absence.

MODULE.NAME: Legacy transition boundary
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Preserve source assignments/owner-stream/messages and opaque historical recipient; classify unambiguous records only after read-only inventory and approved mapping; ambiguous stays isolated; cutover owned by Release Manager.

MODULE.NAME: Transport/validation
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Existing net/http endpoints for new conversation identities after separate API contract approval; validate UTF-8 byte sizes 16384 text, 256 name, JSON body 65536, at most 100 participants and history page 100/default 50.

MODULE.NAME: Document reference
MODULE.RESPONSIBILITY: Store document id/title snapshot in chat messages only; never change Drive ACL or Drive data; opening document remains existing Drive authorization.

FLOW.INVARIANT: Validate caller, canonical pair, uniqueness-enforced get-or-create; reject self-direct.
Group creation and initial owner-membership occur in same transaction; never commit ownerless group.

SEND/JOIN/REMOVE share PostgreSQL conversation transaction gate; REMOVE commits epoch retirement and closes visibility interval. Newly initiated old-epoch notifications after commit denied; already initiated Publish may finish late without sensitive payload. Unsubscribe/disconnect requested after commit.
Transfer owner role atomically to existing eligible member then allow owner leave; never zero/two current owner state at committed boundary.
Validate current actor/membership, deduplicate canonical payload under unique sender+conversation+key, allocate commit-visible message order and commit before best-effort delivery.
Authenticate and scope by current/previous valid membership; cursor strictly progresses over authorized committed ordered messages; never leak absent-interval messages.
Accept only authorized visible marker, update via max(old,new) atomically, sync via committed state to all devices.

OnConnecting and OnSubscribe verify session and current epoch; no sensitive recoverable notifications. Register attempt under PostgreSQL conversation gate while epoch is active, do not hold DB transaction gate while external Publish executes. Pre-REMOVE Publish may finish late, including after timeout UNKNOWN. Rejoin uses fresh opaque epoch channel; HTTP read always reauthorizes.
Inventory/classify in read-only phase, preserve all original data, staged verification and reversibility requirements, Release Manager owns deployment.

DATA_MODEL_CANDIDATES.ENTITY: conversation(conversation_id UUID, kind, created_at, metadata); direct unordered pair has a unique canonical identity; no owner_account_id as conversation identity.
membership(conversation_id, account_id, role, state) and immutable membership interval boundaries over conversation-local committed ordinals; exactly one owner in every committed group state.

message(conversation_id, ordinal, sender_account_id, idempotency_key, canonical payload hash/bytes, body, document_id/title, committed metadata); unique(conversation_id,sender,key); payload mismatch yields 409.
read_state(conversation_id,account_id,last_read_ordinal), nondecreasing; direct visibility state stored per user, not shared.
legacy provenance retains original owner/sender/recipient/idempotency/message IDs/document metadata without silent merge; physical layout deferred to contract/migration stage.

CONCURRENCY_AND_SECURITY.INVARIANT: SEND, JOIN, REMOVE and ownership change have one serialized committed order per conversation. Authorization and assignment of ordinal occur under the same transactional boundary; pending sends after removal commit are rejected.
Exactly one owner exists in any committed group. Transfer is single atomic role transition, never an observable ownerless state. Last owner cannot leave without eligible successor.
A user sees messages only from union of prior/current membership intervals, never during absent intervals; rejoin opens a new interval without backfilling the gap.

REMOVE linearizes at PostgreSQL COMMIT under per-conversation transaction gate protecting SEND/JOIN/TRANSFER, ordinal allocation and membership retirement. Centrifuge Publish is external noncancellable operation: one initiated before REMOVE can be admitted/delivered after REMOVE or caller-side timeout UNKNOWN. Only newly initiated old-epoch Publish after REMOVE must be rejected. Late wake-up and opaque channel IDs reveal no confidential messages, participants, documents or identifiers and convey no access. Never reuse epochs; request unsubscribe/disconnect, but all HTTP/history/fetch reauthorize current session and historic membership intervals. Failed/unknown notification never rolls back persisted message.

The same conversation/sender/key with identical canonical payload replays original result; different canonical payload fails 409 with no write/publish. Commit precedes realtime delivery; publication error never rolls back a message.
Last-read marker is monotonically increasing within visible committed ordinal bounds; own messages and absent intervals do not contribute to unread; multiple devices converge to committed maximum.
All new Chat membership/role decisions are based on valid caller session plus bfe_chat state, not Drive ADMIN or Drive ACL. No changes to Drive APIs, database or permissions.

RESOLUTION.MECHANISM: Introduce conversation UUID and unordered-pair direct uniqueness separate from legacy owner_account_id; legacy streams remain separate read-only identities until classified. Transitional translation cannot silently merge.
RESOLUTION.VERIFICATION: Two concurrent creates return same conversation; ambiguous legacy pair remains unchanged.

RESOLUTION.MECHANISM: Explicit conversation kind/namespace separates legacy ADMIN_READ operations from new membership-only ACL; no fallback ADMIN privileges.
RESOLUTION.VERIFICATION: Drive ADMIN nonmember cannot read, send or subscribe to new conversations.

RESOLUTION.MECHANISM: Variant C: PostgreSQL transaction gate serializes SEND/JOIN/REMOVE/TRANSFER and ordinal; no assumption that gate cancels Centrifuge Publish. Never-reused opaque viewer membership-epoch channels; check epoch before initiating Publish; no new attempt after retirement. An in-flight old-epoch Publish can complete after REMOVE and timeout result is UNKNOWN. No confidential envelope or channel identifiers, no recoverable content; reauthorize every HTTP history read. Revoke requests best-effort unsubscribe/disconnect.
RESOLUTION.VERIFICATION: For PUBLISH→REMOVE, timeout→REMOVE, REMOVE→PUBLISH, CHECK→REMOVE→PUBLISH, REMOVE→REJOIN and failure, prove read-access denial after membership closure, no sensitive envelope/channel leakage, no old-epoch reuse, durable committed messages.

RESOLUTION.MECHANISM: Snapshot/read-only inventory; store immutable source provenance and retain original tables/history; classify with approval gates; quarantine ambiguous legacy records rather than infer direct pairs; rollback retains original API/source.
RESOLUTION.VERIFICATION: Source counts and per-message IDs/keys/doc metadata exactly preserved; ambiguous not merged.

RESOLUTION.MECHANISM: Per-conversation PostgreSQL transaction gate serializes message commits and membership-boundary changes; allocate conversation-local monotone ordinal while holding same lock, and commit with message. Cursor uses ordinal, not global identity/created_at; no holes visible as committed checkpoints.
RESOLUTION.VERIFICATION: Concurrent messages and JOIN/REMOVE yield one stable committed total order; pagination never skips late-committed lower ordinal.

WEBSOCKET_REVOCATION_PROTOCOL.LINEARIZATION: PostgreSQL conversation transaction gate linearizes SEND/JOIN/REMOVE/TRANSFER and ordinal at COMMIT. New notification attempt checks committed active epoch before initiating Publish. No claim that external Centrifuge Publish can be cancelled or linearized at PostgreSQL gate. Publish initiated before REMOVE may complete late; timeout is UNKNOWN, not evidence of non-admission.
WEBSOCKET_REVOCATION_PROTOCOL.TRANSPORT_BOUNDARY: Centrifuge v0.39.3 Node.Publish is synchronous but has no context argument or cancellation guarantee; success signifies broker call completion, not device delivery. Notification contains exactly version and opaque wakeToken, never content, document, sender or protected IDs. Channel names are opaque random unguessable per viewer/epoch and do not reveal private account/conversation IDs. No recoverable publication history. On REMOVE request unsubscribe/disconnect, but security rests on content-free transport and fresh HTTP authorization for each read.
WEBSOCKET_REVOCATION_PROTOCOL.EPOCH_ISOLATION: JOIN produces never-reused epoch and distinct opaque channel. REMOVE retires epoch at commit; no NEW publish or subscription into retired epoch. REJOIN cannot recover prior epoch or read absent membership gaps.
WEBSOCKET_REVOCATION_PROTOCOL.FAILURES: Timeout or ambiguous broker error means UNKNOWN admission, even if an asynchronous wrapper returned. No release of lock is taken as evidence of cancellation; external Publish proceeds outside the PostgreSQL gate. Failed/UNKNOWN realtime notification never undoes committed message; authorized clients resynchronize from PostgreSQL.
WEBSOCKET_REVOCATION_PROTOCOL.ATTEMPT_AUTHORIZATION: Before any external Centrifuge Publish, register an immutable durable attempt record in bfe_chat under the SAME PostgreSQL per-conversation transaction gate used by SEND and REMOVE. Registration references an already COMMITTED message/event, identified by immutable (attemptId UUID, conversationId UUID, viewerId UUID, membershipEpoch never-reused, messageOrdinal bigint, messageId, opaqueWakeToken, opaqueEpochChannelId); these values are fixed at registration and cannot be rebound or updated. Within the lock verify exact committed message belongs to conversation, current viewer membership epoch is active, and messageOrdinal belongs to viewer visibility interval [joinBoundary,leaveBoundary) in the adopted half-open committed ordinal boundary model: ordinal >= joinBoundary and, if closed, ordinal < leaveBoundary. A pending REMOVE cannot interleave registration because it uses the same gate. After REMOVE commits, no attempt may be registered in retired epoch or for a message with ordinal at/after leaveBoundary. A previously registered attempt refers ONLY to that earlier visible message: it cannot be repurposed for a later message M2 even if external Publish finishes after REMOVE. Publication worker atomically and durably transitions REGISTERED to CLAIMED once before invoking Publish outside the PostgreSQL gate; concurrent workers and redelivery cannot execute the same logical attempt again, including when result is UNKNOWN. Timeout/ambiguous broker response sets UNKNOWN, not proof of non-admission; no automatic replay after CLAIMED/UNKNOWN. Durable message remains authoritative, authorized client catches up via HTTP history. Notification transport contains exactly version and unguessable wakeToken, never any binding fields; channel identifiers remain opaque. This is a candidate contract/storage design only, not an approved migration.

SCENARIO.LINEARIZATION_AND_MECHANISM: REGISTER(A,M1) commits under conversation gate before REMOVE(B); M2 commits after boundary B; delayed Publish(A) uses immutable committed M1 binding only.
SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Attempt A cannot address M2 or change viewer/epoch; M2 ordinal at/after leaveBoundary is ineligible for retired epoch.

SCENARIO.LINEARIZATION_AND_MECHANISM: Two workers atomically claim identical durable attemptId; caller timeout yields UNKNOWN after one invocation.
SCENARIO.EXPECTED: At most one logical Node.Publish invocation per attemptId; UNKNOWN not reissued, with authorized history catch-up.

SCENARIO.LINEARIZATION_AND_MECHANISM: Publish begun during active epoch before REMOVE commit.
SCENARIO.EXPECTED: May be delivered after REMOVE, without protected information or access.

SCENARIO.LINEARIZATION_AND_MECHANISM: Publish began before REMOVE, caller timeout UNKNOWN.
SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Possible late broker admission; no protected data or history access.

SCENARIO.LINEARIZATION_AND_MECHANISM: REMOVE committed epoch retirement before new attempt.
Only a Publish begun before REMOVE may complete after; no newly initiated call after retirement.
SEND and REMOVE commit under same PostgreSQL gate.
SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Stable ordinal and membership interval ordering.
No old rights or absent-interval disclosure.

SCENARIO.LINEARIZATION_AND_MECHANISM: Reconnect checks current session and membership.
Message already committed before publication attempt.

WEBSOCKET_REVOCATION_PROTOCOL.CROSS_INVARIANT_CHECK: Conversation order, membership windows, idempotency and cursor remain PostgreSQL transaction-gated and unaffected by asynchronous notification outcome.
